# 99.90 CAD sold for USD and HKD in one transaction, at 1.35 CAD/USD and
# 5.7 HKD/CAD, recorded in USD:
#
#   54.00 CAD -> 40.00 USD          cost 1.35 CAD/USD
#   45.90 CAD -> 261.63 HKD         cost 1/5.7 CAD/HKD
#
# The CAD leaving is worth 74.00 USD, so the entry balances in its own
# currency: -74.00 + 40.00 + 34.00 = 0.
#
# What this fixture produces: two cost bases, each priced by what that split
# alone cost. `fx-balances` on the imported book lists them —
#
#   Assets:Bank:USD     1.35 CAD/USD      40.00 USD    40.00 USD available
#   Assets:Bank:HKD    10/57 CAD/HKD     261.63 HKD   261.63 HKD available
#
# The HKD cost is listed as the fraction it is: 1/5.7 has no exact decimal, and
# a rounded one would not reproduce the amounts it priced.
#
# The point of the three currencies is that neither cost can be had by dividing
# the transaction's CAD by one split's amount: charging the whole 99.90 against
# the USD gives 2.4975, and a rule that only understands the book's currency
# and the split's answers nothing at all for the HKD, since this transaction is
# recorded in USD — a third currency. Both were real defects.
#
# Verified by tests/unit/services/test_cost_of_split.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:HKD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "HKD"

2026-01-05 * "Sell 99.90 CAD for USD and HKD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank -99.90 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "7400/9990"
		value: "-74.00"
	Assets:Bank:USD 40.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "40.00"
	Assets:Bank:HKD 261.63 HKD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "HKD"
		share_price: "3400/26163"
		value: "34.00"
